pages.title: Mobile / Acquisition-to-report overview
pages.intro: Android and iOS use Mobile service boundaries and their own stores/queues. The shared forensic stages begin after acquisition handoff.

notes: Priorities
WhatsApp chats/media, browsing, pictures/videos/audio, downloads/documents and relevant app records are prioritized, then the remaining accessible content is inventoried.
Coverage
A normal unprivileged Android logical pull does not guarantee private databases, encryption keys or deleted bytes. Record actual access and acquired-file counts per family.

pages.title: The 13 controlled stages
pages.intro: The same serial controller governs Mobile evidence after acquisition handoff. One stage owns the job at a time; bounded workers may operate inside a stage.
notes: State meanings

Ready means the configured gates completed. coverage_complete and exception counters still describe missing or inaccessible evidence. A completed acquisition does not prove that every possible artifact was captured.

notes: Platform isolation
Android and iOS jobs stay inside Mobile services. A Mobile job must not be redirected through the Disk runtime merely to bypass an acquisition or parsing error.
Private-data requirement
For inaccessible private apps, use an authorized acquisition that actually contains those databases and matching keys. The application does not root, exploit or unlock a phone.

The current importer does not implement complete encrypted-backup decryption merely because a password is supplied. Use supported external decryption, verify the result, then import plaintext.
Import precision
UFED logical/full-filesystem exports, Android backup and folder imports provide only their included files. A manifest entry with no acquired bytes stays a reference or a coverage gap.

notes: Intake behavior

Auto-capture follows materialization. Capture from case evidence and Upload acquired key file are available in Intake. Existing examiner keys are preserved; captured sources remain available as candidates.
Verification boundary

A 64-character hex value is saved; raw secrets stay out of API metadata, logs and reports. Format validation alone does not prove a matching backup. After extraction, new key files use an explicit Intake upload. crypt15 uses its separate backup-key derivation.

notes: Key formats
A 158-byte Android key file supplies its last 32 bytes (offset 126). Raw 32-byte / 64-hex keys and recognized Java byte-array envelopes are validated.
Crypto boundary

CRYPT15 uses HKDF-SHA256. Every key candidate is tried per source, including Business and Android profiles. Protobuf IVs avoid repeated historical guesses; source/key-set cache avoids repeat decryption.

notes: Deleted photos
A MediaStore trash row with no acquired image bytes is reference-only. A thumbnail is not the original photo. Retained trash files can be linked when their real bytes and hashes exist.
Deleted messages
Residual structures and backup history may yield evidence candidates; they do not guarantee every deleted chat can be recovered. Overwritten, absent or inaccessible encrypted data stays a gap.

Retain artifact ID, original path/hash, model and description. Video evidence also retains decoded presentation time, derived frame PNG and frame hash.

notes: Identity
A chat account, sender, image path or URL links to the actual acquired record. Matching names or filenames remain weaker correlation signals.
Dependency gate
A graph dependency wait holds the serial gate. progressAgent checks the wait reason and retries within policy; it must not report the job ready while the required stage remains waiting.

notes: Acceptance meaning

Pipeline readiness can coexist with source-access gaps. Modern backups require authenticated recovery. Unauthenticated historical results retain their integrity warning. Live acceptance also requires the intended phone bytes and recoverable records.
Historical imports
Reprocess derived stages when a better acquisition or parser becomes available, then generate a new report. Retain the original encrypted backups and historical report runs.

Show the actual retained image or derived frame. Identify thumbnails and recovered candidates. Do not substitute illustrative images for missing evidence.
Alignment
The section uses the same page width, header, watermark, caption and pagination rules as Disk. Device Information and Extraction Summary replace Disk-specific headings.

pages.title: Report / Common section and page structure
pages.intro: The shared renderer keeps the Disk and Mobile report sections aligned. Platform-specific source headings are substituted without changing the surrounding structure.
notes: Shared formatting
A4 page width, section spacing, header, watermark, page numbers, evidence captions and annexure links use the same rendering path.
Content and pagination
Fourteen logical sections are saved in the report run. Evidence volume determines the page count; identical layout does not imply identical length.
Suspicious Activity
This is a dedicated report section and artifact category. It includes source-linked reasons, real retained media or sampled frames, and separate examiner observations.

Use verified source pictures and derived video frame images with captions, artifact IDs, paths/hashes and frame timestamps. Keep examiner observations distinct from model descriptions.

Signal SQLCipher uses its database key and a compatible SQLCipher workflow; encrypted iOS backups use the correct backup/keybag route; archives, Office/PDF and encrypted mail require their specific supported key/password tools.
Device encryption
